text:
incidents-bot: :pager: Paging oncall: detected sudden p99 tail latency spike for router/load-balancer path. Affected: us-west region (primarily us-west-2). Symptoms: streaming stalls, long KV cache waits, elevated queue depth on some backends. Autoscale attempted. PagerDuty: PD#INC-5132. Root thread created at 1789801234.

sre_jordan: I'm taking. What's the current impact window and which routes?

infra-elaine: Observed anomaly starting ~1789801200. Traffic policy 'zone-weight-v2' rolled to us-west canary earlier (rollout id 1789798000). After rollout we see a hot routing skew: a small subset of shards (shard-12/13) getting 60-80% of traffic for several models (model-x, model-chat).

alice: Logs from router node-7: 
```
[1789801215] router: chosen backend shard-12 for model-x (72% of requests) queue_depth=48 avg_service_ms=420
[1789801220] router: backend shard-12 CPU sat, evicting streams -> stalls
[1789801230] stream: stall detected, client-retry x3
```

mg: Any config changes besides the zone-weight rollout? Any infra swaps?

infra-elaine: No infra resizing. Only change was traffic policy rollout and a control-plane patch that adjusted per-zone weights to prefer local availability zones. Looks like the weight calc had an off-by-factor for small zones -> concentrated weights.

alice: Metric snapshot (ago 5m): p95=220ms -> stable, p99=1.8s -> spike. Streaming stall count +42% (mostly for sessions >1k tokens).

mg: OK — immediate mitigation options: 1) revert to consistent-hash-v1 routing policy (fallback) 2) temporarily cap max-connections per backend 3) divert new sessions to warm replica pool in other zones. Which is fastest?

sre_jordan: Revert policy is fastest. infra-elaine, can you patch config to failback to consistent-hash-v1 for affected model routes?

infra-elaine: Running command now: 
```
curl -XPOST https://config-api.internal/v1/policies/apply \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","policy":"consistent-hash-v1","scope":"us-west-2","reason":"emergency rollback - 1789801200"}' 
```

ops-bot: Change submitted: apply-policy 3f7a24. Rolling to 12 nodes in us-west-2. ETA ~45s. :gear:

alice: Seeing immediate drop on new sessions, but existing long-lived streams still stuck on shard-12. We should force-kill stalled streams older than 60s for affected shards to free KV caches.

mg: Agree. Who can run the stream-prune script? Need to be careful with in-flight work. Notify customers first?

pm-raj: We need a short customer impact blurb before any disruptive action. Affected customers: 17 accounts showing >5% error/timeout rate, ~120 req/s impacted. Draft: "We are investigating increased latency and streaming stalls in us-west-2 affecting some generation requests. We are applying a routing rollback and may restart a small number of affected streams to restore capacity. We will update in 30 minutes." Thoughts?

devex-amy: That's fine. Please include that we are not changing model weights or returning degraded outputs — only routing changes and restarts. Notify account teams for the 17 affected.

infra-elaine: Prune script to target shard-12 only: 
```
./scripts/prune_stalled_streams --shard shard-12 --older-than 60
```
Executing...

ops-bot: prune_stalled_streams: 312 streams found, 290 restarted, 22 in-flight kept. avg freed sockets per node=24.

alice: p99 dropping: now 1.1s. p95 steady at 210ms. Streaming stall metric trending down (-65% from peak). Still some tail badness for sessions >2k tokens.

infra-elaine: Confirmed config rollback complete across region. The control-plane patch that computed zone weights had an integer division bug. Will pin and revert that change in the management plane.

sre_jordan: I'll start a brief RCA checklist: capture router allocation maps pre/post, collect shard load histories, check canary rollout logs, reproduce weight calc locally.

oncall-maria: Handoff: I'm taking the remainder of the incident for the next shift. Watching p99 target < 1.2s and streaming-stalls down. If p99>1.5s or any major customer reports >10% error, page me (PD#INC-5132).

mg: Thanks Jordan — good call on rolling back. Can we also enable a temporary per-backend connection cap to avoid re-hotspotting while we fix weight calc?

infra-elaine: Applied soft cap: max_connections_per_backend=250 for shard pool. Should prevent new hot spikes while we rollout a test fix.

alice: Note for runtime team: long sessions accumulate KV cache memory; when a shard is overloaded these sessions are most affected. We should consider softer eviction policies and hotspot detection that migrates sessions gracefully.

pm-raj: Customer impact update draft (for statuspage): "We experienced elevated latency and intermittent streaming stalls in us-west-2 due to an erroneous routing-policy rollout that concentrated traffic onto a small set of backend shards. We rolled back the policy and restarted affected streams; p99 latency has returned near baseline for most traffic. A small subset of long-running sessions may still see degradation; we continue to monitor. No model outputs were altered." Approve?

devex-amy: Approve. I'll notify account teams and paste this to statuspage once we hit stable for 15m.

ops-bot: metric snapshot link: https://metrics.internal/d/routers/p99?from=1789800000&to=1789802400 (auto-scan)

infra-elaine: Post-action items: 1) Rollback control-plane patch from 1789797990 2) Add unit test for zone-weight calc 3) Add canary guard to detect >20% skew on any shard during rollout 4) Improve drain/restart UX for long streams.

sre_jordan: Agreed. Also adding a temp alert to catch >30% of traffic concentrated on any single shard for >2m.

oncall-maria: Taking watch. Leaving PD escalation contact list updated. I will confirm stability in 30m and close the incident if p99 < 1.3s and streaming stall delta < 10% for 30m.

pm-raj: Thanks team. We'll follow up with a postmortem describing the rollout gap and customer comms plan.

incidents-bot: Incident timeline recorded. Severity set to SEV3 -> may escalate based on customer reports. Thread closed for active triage at 1789802400 (monitoring).
